title: His blood be on us, and on our children — the court that owned the blood, and the house that mourns him (Deuteronomy 21; Acts 5; Zechariah 12)
summary:
It ain't new. Pilate washes his hands and the crowd in his court takes the blood on itself:

*When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.* (Matthew 27:24)

*Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.* (Matthew 27:25)

This has been read for seventeen centuries as a curse a whole people laid on its own children. Read what the words were in the Torah. Innocent blood is a charge against the ones who shed it or let it be shed, and the elders of the nearest city answered for it; the prayer was that it not be laid to the people's charge:

*Be merciful, O Yahuah (LORD), unto thy people Yashar'el (Israel), whom thou hast redeemed, and lay not innocent blood unto thy people of Yashar'el's (Israel’s) charge. And the blood shall be forgiven them.* (Deuteronomy 21:8)

Jeremiah said the same to the men who wanted him dead, and the men, not the nation, would carry it:

*But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof: for of a truth Yahuah (LORD) hath sent me unto you to speak all these words in your ears.* (Jeremiah 26:15)

The rulers knew whose charge the blood was. Weeks later, in the same city, they said so to the apostles:

*Saying, Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name? and, behold, ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.* (Acts 5:28)

*Upon us*: the council that tried him. Yahusha (Jesus) had already set the blood where it belonged, on the ones who killed the prophets and would kill him, the rulers of the city, in the same breath that he wept over her:

*That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zechariah son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.* (Matthew 23:35)

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37)

*How often would I have gathered thy children*. The children are the ones he wanted to gather, not the ones cursed. The blood that cries from the ground was Abel's, and it cried against his brother, not against a people:

*And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.* (Genesis 4:10)

And this blood speaks differently from Abel's:

*And to Yahusha (Jesus) the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.* (Hebrews 12:24)

The prophets say what the house that pierced him does with his blood at the end. It mourns him, the same house, and a third of it is left:

*And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.* (Zechariah 12:10)

*And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Yahuah (LORD), two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.* (Zechariah 13:8)

The blood fell on the court that owned it and on the city that stood in it forty years later. It is not a curse on the people of Yahudah (Judah) or on their children. The same people are the house of David that looks on him whom they pierced and mourns.

3135.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) is speaking to the scribes and the rulers, and he says some of the ones he sends they will *kill and crucify*. The crowd in Pilate's court taking the blood on itself is the same hand he was already naming. The charge sits on the system that kills the sent ones, not on a people.
3135.phrase: some of them ye shall kill and crucify
3135.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names who will kill and crucify the ones he sends: the scribes and rulers he is addressing.

3136.prose: He weeps over the city and says how often he would have gathered her children. Those children are the ones he wanted under his wings, so the cry about *our children* cannot be a curse on them. The killers he names are the rulers; the children are the lost sheep he came for.
3136.phrase: how often would I have gathered thy children together
3136.sentence: The children he longed to gather are the ones the crowd names, so they are the ones he sought, not the ones he cursed.

3137.prose: Right after the charge on the rulers, Yahusha (Jesus) leaves the temple, and what he says next is its ruin. The fall comes on the house and its keepers, the court that owned the blood, in the city that stood in it. It lands on the place, not on the children of Yahudah (Judah) as a people.
3137.phrase: went out, and departed from the temple
3137.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) walks out of the temple, and what follows is the fall of that house, which is where the blood comes to rest.

3138.prose: The apostles pray David's words over what happened in Pilate's court. The raging and the vain imagining belong to those gathered against the Father's anointed: Herod and Pilate, the rulers, and the crowd they drew in. It is a court's doing, and they pray it as a charge against the powers, not a curse on a people.
3138.phrase: Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things
3138.sentence: David's words about the raging gathering are what the apostles say was happening against Yahusha (Jesus), a gathering of rulers and the crowd they moved.

3140.prose: Jeremiah told the men who wanted him dead that killing him would bring *innocent blood upon yourselves*, and upon the city. The weight falls on the ones who do it. In the next breath the people themselves say he is not worthy to die. The cry in Pilate's court is the rulers' charge being taken up, the same one Jeremiah named.
3140.phrase: ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves
3140.sentence: The prophet puts the innocent blood on the men who would kill him, not on the whole nation.

3141.prose: Sailors from the nations knew what innocent blood was. Before they threw Jonah in, they begged Yahuah (LORD) not to *lay* it on them. Pilate washes his hands and the court takes the blood on itself, which is the Torah's weight turned around. The old prayer was always that it not be laid on anyone's charge.
3141.phrase: lay not upon us innocent blood
3141.sentence: Men who knew blood was a charge asked that none be laid on them, the plain background to the cry in Pilate's court.

3142.prose: A man is found slain and no one knows who did it. The Torah does not blame the people at large. The elders and judges of the nearest city answer for the blood, and they pray that it not be laid on Yashar'el (Israel). So blood is a charge on the court and its keepers, which is where Pilate's crowd and rulers stand.
3142.phrase: lying in the field, and it be not known who hath slain him
3142.sentence: A slain man whose killer is unknown puts the blood on the nearest city's elders, which is how the Torah treats innocent blood.

3143.prose: Abel's blood cried out, and it cried against his brother. Yahuah (LORD) asks the killer, *What hast thou done?* Blood speaks against the hand that shed it, never against a people. Pilate's court is that kind of case, with the weight on the ones who shed it or let it be shed.
3143.phrase: the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground
3143.sentence: Blood that cries from the ground cries against the killer, and here the killer is Cain, one man, not a people.

3145.prose: The house that pierced him is the house that mourns him. Yahuah (LORD) pours out *the spirit of grace* on the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, and they look on him and mourn as for an only son. That is what becomes of the same people, so the blood cannot end as their curse.
3145.phrase: they shall look upon me whom they have pierced
3145.sentence: The ones who pierced him are the ones who look on him and mourn, so the blood ends in grace on that house, not a curse.

3146.prose: Two parts cut off and one third left. The judgment on the land is hard, but it is not the end, and a remnant is kept. Read beside the blood, the cost falls on the many who stood in the system, while the house that is left is still the house that mourns him.
3146.phrase: two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein
3146.sentence: Two parts are cut off but a third is left, so the judgment is not the end of the people.

3147.prose: The one the court shed blood of was *wounded for our transgressions*. The same blood the rulers took on themselves is borne for the ones who went astray, the lost sheep of Yashar'el (Israel). So the blood of this just person was not aimed at the people. It was carried for them.
3147.phrase: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed
3147.sentence: His stripes bring healing to the ones he bled for, which turns the blood in Pilate's court into peace for the people.

5335.prose: On the Day of Atonement two are taken. One is sent away into the wilderness with the people's sins on its head, and one is given up. Pilate sets two before the crowd as well, Barabbas let go and Yahusha (Jesus) delivered. The sins are confessed over the goat, so the guilt has a named place to rest.
5335.phrase: confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)
5335.sentence: On the day of atonement the sins are confessed over the live goat that is sent away, as Barabbas is sent away and Yahusha (Jesus) is delivered.

5336.prose: Pilate delivers Yahusha (Jesus) when he has scourged him, and Isaiah had said it long before: *with his stripes we are healed*. The scourging is the wounding for the transgressions of the people. He bears it, and it is not laid on them.
5336.phrase: he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities
5336.sentence: Isaiah names the wounding and bruising that Pilate's scourging carries out, and says it is borne for the people's sins.
